newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says end "toxic atmosphere" in capital.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says end "toxic atmosphere" in capital.

text.p: President Clinton Thursday led the country's leading politicians in a prayer that they root out a "toxic atmosphere of cynicism" that is choking the capital.

"This town is ripped with people who are self-righteous, sanctimonious and hypocritical. All of us are that way sometime. I plead guilty from time to time," Clinton told a national prayer breakfast attended by many members of Congress, including House Speaker Newt Gingrich and House Democratic Leader Dick Gephardt.
In a similar vein, Hillary Rodham Clinton told the prayer service later in the day, "We have spent too much time in the last few years demonising people with whom we do not agree politically."

Mrs. Clinton, who has been a lightning rod for criticism from conservative groups, said a man whom she did not identify approached her Wednesday night at a dinner for the people hosting the prayer service.

"Last night a man came up to me and said to me, 'Mrs. Clinton, please forgive me. For the last four years I have worked very hard to destroy you.' I told him, 'Of course I forgive you,'" the first lady said.
The Clintons were picking up on a theme the president talked about during his Jan. 20 inaugural address and again in his State of the Union speech Tuesday night.

Citing a Bible passage from the prophet Isaiah, Clinton said Americans need to come together across the racial and ethnic spectrum and become "repairers of the breach." He said Washington's politicians and press "are in the breach and are in a deep hole and need to be lifted up."
A particular affliction in Washington is the enormous amount of time spent trying to get even with political enemies, Clinton said, adding that he succumbed to the temptation in the past.
"I'd wake up the morning, my heart was getting a little harder," he said. "It's not a very pleasant way to live frankly -- not even any fun."

Now, he said, "I try to tell everybody around the White House all the time (that) I have concluded a few things in my life, and one of them is that you don't ever get even. The harder you try, the more frustrated you're going to be, because nobody ever gets even. And when you do, you're not really happy. You don't feel fulfilled."

Leading the group assembled in a downtown hotel in prayer, Clinton said: "Pray for the people in public office that we can rid ourselves of this toxic atmosphere of cynicism, and embrace with joy and gratitude this phenomenal opportunity and responsibility before us."
Clinton has made bipartisanship a key objective in the early days of his second four-year term.

So far there have been no serious political disputes between the Republican-controlled Congress and the Democratic president but a probe into Democratic campaign fund-raising is likely to generate ill will.

Clinton has fretted about the political atmosphere in Washington since his early days here, particularly after boyhood friend Vince Foster, then a White House deputy counsel, died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound and left a note that said, "Here, ruining people is considered sport."

At the prayer breakfast, Gingrich, recently fined $300,000 for ethics abuses that Democrats sought to topple him for, gave a New Testament reading from the Book of John. Gephardt gave the Old Testament reading, from the Book of Psalms.
The whole group joined together in singing "Amazing Grace" at the end.
